How like these two are to two brothers who inherited from their father a piece of land that needed work and cultivation. They divided it into two halves; they had nothing besides it. One of them was intelligent and resolute, the other to the opposite. The intelligent one saw that occupying himself with his land alone would cut him off from contriving for his livelihood and procuring his sustenance, so he hired himself out in the working of another's land, that he might live from the wage of his work day by day. And whenever he was released from his work for another at the evening of his day, he seized his moment — an hour from it — and worked his land with diligence and energy. And whenever he had a surplus from his wages — of a day's sustenance or more — he left off working for another for that period, and worked his land with the utmost of his strength and energy. He continued so until he completed the work of his land in the most fitting manner; and when the time of its yield arrived and the season of its produce came, he gathered it and harvested it, and lived from it through the whole of his second year. He worked his land with intelligence, and never ceased increasing its yield until its produce sufficed for his sustenance — and there was a surplus left him, by which he could add to his land beyond his own.

But the ignorant brother — when he knew that working his land would cut him off from earning what would sustain him — abandoned it altogether and was heedless of it; and then he hired himself out to people in working land, took his wages, lived from them, and was sustained by them, but achieved nothing from them beyond his food and bare subsistence. When the food of his day was in surplus, he made of it a day of leisure and ease and recreation, and did not think of the matter of his land. He took his pleasure in the bathhouse in the times when there was surplus left him in his working-days. So his land remained idle, growing nothing — rather, thorns grew up on it, its hedges fell in ruin, and the torrents carried away its fruit — as the Wise One said: "I passed by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding; and lo, it was all grown over with thorns, the face of it was covered with nettles, and the stone wall of it was broken down" (Proverbs 24:30–31).

The intelligent man, when he sees this parable with his reason, reflects through it on the matters of his next world — which is his house in true reality — and works for it with all his diligence; and when he works for his this-world, he works for it as one who works in the land of another, only according to necessity and need. The ignorant one acts in the two matters to the opposite — he toils in the matters of his this-world and is heedless of the matters of his next world — like the saying of the Wise One in his reflection upon the ignorant man: "I beheld, and laid it to my heart; I saw and received instruction" (Proverbs 24:32).

As for how many kinds of traces of wisdom there are in the created things, by which we may reflect —

וְסִימָנֵי הַחָכְמָה בְּכָל זֶה עַל ג׳ עִנְיָנִים.

הָא׳ מֵהֶם סִימָנִים מְבֹאָרִים וּגְלוּיִים אֵינָם נֶעֱלָמִים מִן הַכְּסִילִים כ״ש מִן הַמַּשְׂכִּילִים כִּתְנוּעַת גַּלְגַּל הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ מִמַּעַל לָאָרֶץ בַּיּוֹם לְהָאִיר פְּאַת הַיִּשּׁוּב וְיֵהָנוּ בָּהּ הַבְּרוּאִים כמ״ש הַכָּתוּב (תהלים קד) תִּזְרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יֵאָסֵפוּן וְגוֹ׳ יֵצֵא אָדָם לְפָעֳלוֹ וְלַעֲבֹדָתוֹ עֲדֵי עָרֶב מָה רַבּוּ מַעֲשֶׂיךָ ה׳ כֻּלָּם בְּחָכְמָה עָשִׂיתָ וְגוֹ׳.

וְהַשֵּׁנִית סִימָנִים נֶעֱלָמִים מִן הַבְּרוּאִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵדַע פִּשְׁרָם כִּי אִם הַמַּשְׂכִּיל הַמֵּבִין יָשְׁרָם כַּמָּוֶת הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל בָּשָׂר וּבוֹ תַּקָּנַת הָעוֹלָם כמ״ש זַ״ל (בראשית א׳:ל״א) וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד זֶה הַמָּוֶת וְאָמַר הֶחָכָם (קהלת י) וְשַׁבֵּחַ אֲנִי אֶת הַמֵּתִים שֶׁכְּבָר מֵתוּ מִן הַחַיִּים אֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה חַיִּים עֲדֶנָה.

וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי סִימָנֵי הֶחָכְמָה שֶׁהֵם נִרְאִים מִצַּד א׳ וְנֶעֱלָמִים מִצַּד א׳ וְלֹא יַכִּירֵם מִי שֶׁבִּינָתוֹ מְעוּטָה אֶלָּא לְאַחַר שֶׁהִתְיַשֵּׁב בָּהֶם וִידַקְדֵּק עֲלֵיהֶם כְּהִשְׁתַּנּוּת עִנְיְנֵי הַשָּׁנָה בְּאַרְבַּע תְּקוּפוֹתֵיהֶם וְהַדּוֹמֶה לָזֶה.
